title: Check-raising and playing out of position
summary: The main weapon out of position: when and with what to check-raise.

idea.text: A **check-raise** is a check followed by a raise after the opponent bets. Out of position you act first and see less; a check-raise lets you build a big pot when it suits you and punish an opponent who bets too often.

with-what.text:
What to check-raise with:
- **For value**: sets, two pair, strong top pair on wet boards that need protection.
- **As a semi-bluff**: strong draws, especially combo draws (flush draw plus straight draw) with lots of outs.

Don't check-raise middle pairs: the opponent's strong hands won't fold, and their weak ones you already beat.

labels: A set of sevens: a value check-raise
A combo draw: 15 outs, a semi-bluff check-raise

q-cr.q: Which hand suits a check-raise worst on K♠ 8♦ 3♣?
q-cr.explain: A middle pair loses to the hands that call a raise and gains nothing by raising the weak ones.

options: Checking, then raising after the opponent bets
t1.explain: A check-raise is checking first, then raising the opponent's bet.

t2.q: Which draw is best for a semi-bluff check-raise?
t2.explain: The more outs, the more often a semi-bluff wins even when called.

t3.q: Why does the out-of-position player need the check-raise?
options: To grow the pot with strong hands and punish frequent bets
t3.explain: The check-raise gives the out-of-position player a way to win more and keep the opponent's aggression in check.
